D.quote: Today, we commemorate the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks on our country which claimed the lives of 2,977 people and injured thousands of others.
Today, Durbin attended the City of Chicago Fire Department’s 9/11 Tribute, marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.

[CHICAGO, IL] — Combat Veteran and U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth, a member of the U.S. Senate Armed Services Committee (SASC) who served in the Reserve Forces for 23 years, today joined volunteers at Chicago Union Station to help pack 520,000 meals that will be donated to the Greater Chicago Food Depository as part of a day of service commemorating the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.

R.quote: Today, on the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks, Congressman Rick W. Allen (GA-12) attended the annual 9/11 Remembrance Ceremony and Memorial Stair Climb in Evans, Georgia.

– Today, U.S. Senator Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.) released a video marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11th terror attacks and honoring the victims, their families, the first responders, and the service members who answered the call.

AUGUSTA, ME – U.S. Senator Susan Collins delivered remarks today at the Maine Firefighters Memorial in Augusta during a ceremony marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.

D.quote: Twenty-five years ago, our nation was forever changed by the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001.
Twenty-five years ago, today, the United States of America experienced one of its darkest days in history.
Twenty-five years ago today, I vividly recall looking down the National Mall from the Capitol Building and watching as black smoke billowed up from the Pentagon.

R.quote: Twenty-five years ago, America suffered the deadliest foreign attack on American soil in our nation’s history.
Twenty-five years ago, America’s strength was tested.
Twenty-five years ago today, America faced an unimaginable tragedy, and our nation was forever changed.

D.quote: Our solemn commemoration keeps alive the memory of those who were lost and honors the first responders who selflessly put themselves in harm’s way to protect others and save lives.
We also honor the extraordinary courage of the first responders who rushed toward danger and helped save countless lives.
Seeing the towers collapse, the imagery of the towers collapse, and the first responders who gave their lives.

R.quote: Today, we remember the lives of those who died on September 11, 2001 from terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center in New York City, the Pentagon in Virginia, on United Airlines Flight 93 which crashed in rural Pennsylvania, and the first responders who charged toward the chaos as others fled to safety.

– Today, U.S. Senator Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.) released a video marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11th terror attacks and honoring the victims, their families, the first responders, and the service members who answered the call.
We honor the first responders who ran toward danger, the brave passengers and crew of Flight 93 who sacrificed their lives to save others, and the many others who stepped up to help our nation.

D.quote: Today, let us keep all of those we lost in our thoughts, let us pray for their families and loved ones, and let us hold true to the words “we will never forget.
But something else happened in those days that I will never forget: America came together.

R.quote: Twenty-five years later, our promise remains the same: We will never forget.
A quarter-century has passed, but our promise remains the same: we will never forget the lives taken from us, and we will never forget the quiet strength and goodness that brought us through.

D.quote: As we mark the 25th anniversary of 9/11, we will remember the nearly 3,000 people who were killed, and the countless families whose lives were changed forever.

Twenty-five years later, I’m praying for the families of the nearly 3,000 Americans who died, the first responders who heroically put themselves in harm’s way in the aftermath, the thousands of Americans who suffered disability or death because of the dangerous recovery work, the tens of thousands of servicemembers who answered the call and defended our nation in the War on Terror, and the millions of ordinary Americans who pulled together to try and help the nation heal.
Twenty-five years later, we remember the nearly 3,000 people who lost their lives and the families and loved ones whose lives were forever changed.

R.quote: Today on the 25th anniversary, we remember the nearly 3,000 innocent lives taken from us, and we continue to pray for the families and loved ones who have carried that loss.

Tucson, AZ - U.S. Representative Juan Ciscomani is commemorating the 25th anniversary of September 11, 2001 today in remembering the nearly 3,000 Americans who lost their lives, honoring the survivors who continue to carry the scars of that day, and recognizing the brave law enforcement officers, firefighters, first responders, and ordinary Americans who ran toward danger when our nation needed them most.

Chairman Garbarino is committed to honoring the nearly 3,000 people killed, including almost 500 Long Islanders, recognizing the heroism of first responders and civilians, and ensuring younger generations and future national security leaders understand the significance of 9/11 and why continued commitment to the homeland security mission is as important as ever.
